biography.value:
Background

Gren Greenmantle was born to a warren of forest gnomes hidden in the Misty Woods, and from the first his gift ran toward life: the rare silver-white spellfire in his hands drank in raw magic, but where it touched living things it closed wounds and coaxed green shoots from bare ground.

Fearing what such a power might draw down on a hidden warren, the elders sent him north to a shrine of life in Daggerford, where the acolytes tamed the wild flame into a healer's discipline and taught him that preserving life was a calling worth the risk of wielding it.

It was there, copying an old ledger leaf by candlelight, that he first read the name of the Broken Heart — and understood what a healer's hands could do to every living thing between Daggerford and the deep wood.

He first met Morgash the Gravemaker on a caravan run south of the town, when a guard took a wound the old orc already had a grave measured for — until Gren's silver fire closed it and set the man back on his feet. Now Gren rides south at the gravedigger's shoulder, healer to Morgash's blade, half-hoping the same quiet thing the orc does: that a heart broken into pieces can be gathered up and made whole again.

Appearance

Physical: Male · forest gnome · white hair swept back from his brow · full white beard and moustache · weathered sun-browned skin, deeply lined · sharp focused eyes under heavy dark brows · short and compact.

He wears layered deep-green robes with gold filigree embroidery at the collar and cuffs, brown leather belt pouches, and carries a gnarled wooden staff topped with a green crystal. His spellfire shows as a wisp of cool silver-white flame cupped in an open palm.

An acorn from the heart-oak at the center of a hidden warren in the Misty Forest, pressed into Gren’s hand by the elders the day they sent him north. It has stayed green and living for years without soil, and it warms faintly in his palm whenever his spellfire flows.

Warren tradition says you plant it when you find the place you’re meant to stay. Gren hasn’t yet.

The tiny left mitten Gren wore the day his spellfire first woke. The silver-white flame passed clean through the wool without charring a thread — instead the scorch spread through the weave like a flower pressed in cloth.

His mother kept it all the years he was growing; the elders returned it to him when he left, so he’d remember his fire was never made to burn.

A single folded page in Gren’s own careful hand — his practice copy of an old temple ledger, made the day he found the line about the Broken Heart. The entry is transcribed exactly, with one small marginal note in gnomish shorthand: “four shards — who else has read this?”

The crease lines say it’s been unfolded and refolded a hundred times.

items.name: The Bolt That Missed Its Grave

description.value:
A bent crossbow bolt with a dark-stained tip, cut out of a caravan guard south of Daggerford — a wound Morgash had already measured a grave for, until Gren’s silver fire closed it. The old orc handed him the bolt without a word.

Gren keeps it as a plain answer to what his fire is for: this one didn’t get a grave.

You touch one Large or smaller object that isn’t being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like.

Covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to cast it without any Verbal, Somatic, or Material components, except Material components that are consumed by the spell or that have a cost specified in the spell.

description.value:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

This small sphere of thick glass weighs 1 pound. If you are within 60 feet of it, you can command it to emanate light equivalent to that of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDaylight00]{Daylight} spell (your choice). Once used, the Daylight effect can’t be used again until the next dawn.

You can issue another command as a Magic action to make the illuminated globe rise into the air and float no more than 5 feet off the ground. The globe hovers in this way until you or another creature grasps it. If you move more than 60 feet from the hovering globe, it follows you until it is within 60 feet of you. It takes the shortest route to do so. If prevented from moving, the globe sinks gently to the ground and becomes inactive, and its light winks out.

An @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagArcaneFocus]{Arcane Focus} is bejeweled or carved to channel arcane magic. A Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard can use such an item as a Spellcasting Focus.
A Bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature. While in a Bedroll, you automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold (see the Dungeon Master ’s Guide).

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

Dice winnings. The man who lost it swore its luck was all used up. Every day since has suggested otherwise.

While this polished agate is on your person, you gain a +1 bonus to ability checks and saving throws.

Wand, Uncommon

This wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can expend no more than 3 charges to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile} from it. For 1 charge, you cast the level 1 version of the spell. You can increase the spell’s level by 1 for each additional charge you expend.

Regaining Charges. The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand’s last charge, roll [[/r 1d20]]. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement by a Spellcaster)

While this pearl is on your person, you can take a Magic action to regain one expended spell slot of level 3 or lower. Once you use the pearl, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

As a Utilize action, you can use Manacles to bind an unwilling Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. While bound, a creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls, and the creature is Restrained if the Manacles are attached to a chain or hook that is fixed in place. Escaping the Manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check as an action. Bursting them requires a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check as an action.

Each set of Manacles comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use Thieves’ Tools to pick the Manacles’ lock with a successful [[/tool thief dex 15]] check.
For 1 hour, a lit Candle sheds Bright Light in a 5-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 5 feet.
A Glass Bottle holds up to 1½ pints.
A Flask holds up to 1 pint.
A Vial holds up to 4 ounces.

Staff, very rare (requires attunement by a Cleric, Sorcerer, or Wizard)

This staff can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. While holding it, you also gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.

Spells. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: Darkness (2 charges), Invisibility (2 charges), Dispel Magic (3 charges), or Counterspell (3 charges).

effects.name: Protection from Death
effects.description:
The first time the target would drop to 0 Hit Points before the spell ends, the target instead drops to 1 Hit Point, and the spell ends.

If the spell is still in effect when the target is subjected to an effect that would kill it instantly without dealing damage, that effect is negated against the target, and the spell ends.
